newsitem.title: CHINA: Survey finds growing wealth gap in Chinese capital.
newsitem.headline: Survey finds growing wealth gap in Chinese capital.

text.p: The disparity in assets between rich and poor families in Beijing has widened as private sector growth rapidly outpaces that of wheezing state industries, the China Daily said on Wednesday.

A survey of 1,550 urban households in the Chinese capital found that families with incomes in the top 20 percent owned 44.8 percent of total household assets in the city while those in the bottom 20 percent owned just 5.7 percent, the newspaper said.
"Differences in property holdings between rich and poor families in Beijing have been enlarged by the widening gap between their incomes," the newspaper said.

Households with members who worked for foreign-funded firms, private companies or were self-employed had the most possessions while those with members who worked for loss-making companies or who were retired had the fewest, it said.
Most of China's loss-making firms belong to the ailing state sector, which has been increasingly outpaced by the private sector boom's during nearly two decades of market-oriented economic reforms.
The value of property held by families in Beijing was estimated at more than 164.9 billion yuan ($19.86 billion), the newspaper said.
Bank savings, securities and cash accounted for 58 percent of the value of assets held by urban families, it said.
The other 42 percent of household assets was made up of physical property such as housing, gold and silver, vehicles and other possessions.
Paramount leader Deng Xiaoping swept aside strict communist policies when he launched economic reforms in the late 1970s.
China has hundreds of thousands of state enterprises, of which officials say 70 percent are in the red and 40 percent suffer chronic deficits.
